content:
In his latest speech, Trump provided his critics with a ready-made viral moment by ignoring context.

Speaking at a union on Tuesday where he was announcing a government rollout of a new AI-powered America.gov website, the President said "unrivaled," and claimed "some of my friends, serious high-tech people, they've seen this thing over the last few days, they can't believe it."

Trump continued: "They say, 'It's one of the most incredible things your government has ever done.' I don't think so. I think it's very good. But somebody said, 'Sir, this is going to be the most significant thing you've ever done in government.' I said, 'I don't think so, but it's very good, okay?' It's just another thing, another thing."

Trump quoted back: 'Sir, sir, undoubtedly, this will be the most significant thing you've ever done—'

Trump then returned to his own voice to say: "If this were really the most significant thing I've ever done, then I'm doing a terrible job as president, I'll tell you. But you know what, it's very good."

Trump was apparently trying to express that if this new website—a digital gateway to government services that has also overturned his false claims about the 2020 election—was his greatest achievement, then his overall performance in office would be a failure.

But "I'm doing a terrible job as president" was quickly clipped and went viral on social media, unsurprisingly becoming a runaway hit.
